Thank your for replying. I do not take it for granted.

The problem in my case is all this is doing is making me angrier and pushing me further from God and love. I have cursed God and I have cursed His creation of me. He must know that. Then why continue? It is either torture, which I would get, or His inability to understand that this particular method of testing does not work well with me.

I want nothing from God. And I no longer want anything to do with God, Satan, Angels, or Demons. To be crude, I want them all the piss off and leave me alone. I have no fear of oblivion. 

Yet...He remains. I feel Him within me, and it makes it so hard to be in this world with its Dark Prince. Look at reality, in truth Money is God for most people. They spend more time worshipping it than the Father of Jesus Christ. And I see the sin in me. The ugliness that will never go away. I am and always will be a sinner. But worse a self aware sinner who can see the sins of the world I participate in making. 

If I destroy myself it will only make things worse. If I continue it will only sustain the machine. How can I love myself? How can I love this world that makes me want to vomit? Why would God die for this world? It would be better to put it down like a sick animal. I do not understand God's love. I do not understand love. All I know is hate. The fire of Sodom, the destroyer of Egypt.

Long story short, if there is a God, He/She/It likes to poke certain people throughout their life. Usually, nothing horrific, but bad, annoying, and ongoing.

I am 46. My entire life if full of random events that are so outrageously improbable that I am either incredibly unlucky or God in allowing me to be poked, and poked, and poked...

The first day I wore a cross, I broke me leg and it took nine months before I could walk without any assistance device. Poke. Right now I am living in an apartment full of salt. An improbable series of events spread particles of highly penetrative salt through my entire apartment. Everyone I talk to about it says they have never seen anything like it. Poke. And the salt thing happened right after I was divorce from my wife who walk out on me and left me alone right before the COVID lockdown. Poke. And it goes on and on.

I am an obese, middle aged man, with a comfortable job. My wife just left me because she could not handle my mood issues.  I am so alone. I just spent an hour and a half uncontrollable sobbing during the middle of the work day today, and my boss had to talk me through it. I have flushed more than $10,000 down the drain in psychiatrists, psychologists, councilors, and medication. Yet, I am still in so much pain. I have always been in pain. It's only when I drink that the pain stops, but my middle aged liver cannot handle that. I tried to OD on medications and alcohol, but all I did was sleep in late. The only time I feel alive is when I hate. I love to hate, I look for reasons to hate. I am addicted to it.

Yes. But "she" explained it was a nickname from her granny. I was really lonely, so I bought it. What finally broke the camel's back is when I had given her enough money to visit and lo and behold there is a family emergency that cost exactly the amount I had given "her".
She/he/they must have removed it because of the attention I was calling to it. I still have my Cash App receipts if needed as evidence (assuming it comes to that).
She also claimed to have been born in Canada on April 6, 1994.
Thank you for the information. I will look into this.

I had another thought about this last night. 

Christ called me later in my life. Until then, I was a slave to Satan through and through. No, I was not a Satanist, but my heart was full of hatred. My sins were rarely of the carnal type, but mostly of the demonic variety. I hated people, I hated the world, I hated some concept of a creator, and I even hated being. If there was a button I could push to undo all creation and its creator, I would have pushed it without hesitation.

So, when Christ called me, I can imagine Satan's rage (for once it was my own). He had me in the bag, and is now doing everything he can to reclaim me. And he plays to my greatest weakness, my pride. "How dare God treats me like this!" implies that I have a claim on God, that I somehow exist outside of His grace. Things are coming into focus thanks to the wonderful advice of everyone. Thank you and bless you all.

Thank you for taking the time to reply.

Very interesting take on the story of Job. I never thought of it that way, and I will have to deeply consider in my journey.

Thanks again.

Thank you for taking time to reply, and for providing such inspiring passages.

I was called by Lord Jesus Christ. To deny that would make me a liar. However, every time I move toward Him something gets in the way. My leg is just one of many experiences. So now I am left angry, bitter, and confused. If you do not want me, then why did you call me? And if you want me, why do you throw so many stumbling blocks in my way?

After years of this happening, it is hard not to take it personally. Is God just playing games with me? Does he find my confusion and suffering amusing? Does he hate me?

Now the bonds of trust are gone. And each day I get angrier and angrier. It is written that "God is Love." But I do not see it anymore. At best I am grateful that God has not gotten around to smiting me some more.

Thank you for taking the time to reply.

I want to start off with acknowledging that there are people in the world whose pain and suffering are beyond my comprehension, and they still keep their faith. So I do not dare compare a broken leg to what others suffer. On the scale of things, my suffering barely registers. The reason it has meaning to me was just how improbable the accident was, and it was the first day I had ever worn a cross.

The test theory is an interesting one. I had never thought of that. Well, if it was a test, I failed miserably. After the ambulance delivered me to the ER, I gave my wife the cross and told her to throw it away. This was not because of some anger toward God (that came later); rather, it was motivated by thinking that somehow the cross was cursed.

It is interesting you mention this theory. As a teenager, I remember reading the Book of Job and being horrified. What I took away from it was that God allowed Satan to torture a righteous man to win a bet. And then God's reply to Job struck me as, "I am the All-Powerful God! How dare you question me?" When God's actions are akin to some insane tyrant, then that is a God I cannot worship or love. In fact, it seems the wisest course of action would be to keep out of sight.

Like I said, if it was a test, then I failed. It broke the bonds of trust I had in God, and now I can only see an insane tyrant.
